Exam preparation

Preparation built around the real patterns of tamam bare sarkari tests — SPSC, FPSC, PPSC aur IBA Sukkur STS. Har test subject-wise hison mein banta hai: English, GK, current affairs, Pakistan studies, Islamiyat, mathematics, general science aur computer. Neeche har subject ki tafseel aur practice di hai.

English · 20 MCQs

English

Grammar, vocabulary, synonyms and antonyms, prepositions, sentence correction and comprehension — the highest-scoring section when practised daily.

Practice now →
Mathematics · 25 MCQs

Mathematics

Percentage, ratio and proportion, averages, sets, basic algebra and geometry — with shortcut methods for solving under time pressure.

Practice now →
General science · 25 MCQs

General science

Everyday physics, chemistry and biology from the Sindh textbook board syllabus — plants, the human body, energy, matter and the solar system.

Practice now →
GK and Pakistan studies · 15 MCQs

Pakistan studies, GK and Islamiyat

Pakistan movement, constitution, geography, current affairs 2025–26 and Islamiyat essentials — the facts that repeat in almost every paper.

Practice now →
Mother tongue · 15 MCQs

Sindhi and Urdu

Grammar, idioms, proverbs and literature in your mother tongue — an easy-scoring section most candidates leave until the last week.

Get the notes →
EST · BS-16

EST and teaching licence

EST is a separate BS-16 post under the Teaching Licence Policy 2023 — filled 30 percent through SPSC, 50 percent by promotion from JEST and 20 percent from PST. The STEDA licence test weighs subject content 40 percent and pedagogy 60 percent.

Get the notes →

Papers — quick jump

Is page par teen hisay hain — real papers, model papers aur organisation-wise papers. Kisi bhi hisay par seedha jayein:

Honest labels: "Model paper" matlab practice ke liye banaya gaya paper hai jo official pattern par hai — asal exam paper nahi. Jahan "real past paper" likha hai, wahi asal guzishta paper hai.

Solved Model Papers by Organization

Saat bare idaron ke liye MR Academy ke tayyar karda model / practice papers — har idare ke official test pattern par, 100 solved MCQs ke saath. Sach ye hai ke in commissions ki official websites par past papers download ke liye mojood nahi hain, is liye ye papers honestly "Model Paper" likh kar diye ja rahe hain — pattern bilkul asli test jesa. Inhi 700 sawalon ko Test Centre ke bank mein bhi shamil kar diya gaya hai, taa ke 20 / 50 / 100 sawalon ke online tests bhi chalein.

Lesson 1 — HTML: your first web pageHTML

HTML is the skeleton of every web page. Tags tell the browser what each part of the page is.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head><title>My first page</title></head>
  <body>
    <h1>Assalam-o-Alaikum</h1>
    <p>This is my first web page.</p>
  </body>
</html>

<h1> is a big heading, <p> is a paragraph. Almost every tag opens and closes — what goes between them is the content.

Lesson 2 — CSS: making pages clear and readableCSS

CSS controls how a page looks — colours, sizes, spacing and layout.

h1 { color: #166649; }
p { font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.6; }

Each rule names an element, then lists its styles inside curly brackets.

Lesson 3 — C++: variables and outputC++

C++ is the language taught in most Pakistani universities. A variable is a named box that stores a value.

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;
int main() {
    int marks = 85;
    cout << "My marks are " << marks;
    return 0;
}

int stores whole numbers, cout prints to the screen.

Lesson 4 — Python: a friendly startPython

Python reads almost like English, which makes it a good first language for data science and AI.

name = "MR Academy"
marks = [80, 75, 90, 88]
average = sum(marks) / len(marks)
print(name, "your average is", average)

No semicolons, no curly brackets — just clean, readable code.

Lesson 5 — C++: variables and data typesC++

A variable is a named box in memory where your program stores a value. Before you use a variable in C++, you must declare it with a data type. The type tells the computer what kind of value the box will hold, and how much memory it needs.

The common types are simple: int for whole numbers, double for decimal numbers, char for one character, string for text, and bool for true or false. Choose the right type for your data. For example, age is an int, price is a double, and a student name is a string.

#include <iostream>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    int age = 22;
    double marks = 69.5;
    string name = "Ali";
    bool passed = true;

    cout << name << " is " << age << " years old." << endl;
    cout << "Marks: " << marks << endl;
    return 0;
}

Remember two good habits: give variables clear names like totalMarks, and give them a starting value when you create them. This makes your code easy to read and avoids strange mistakes.

Lesson 6 — C++: loops made easyC++

A loop repeats a block of code many times, so you do not have to write the same line again and again. If you want to print numbers from 1 to 100, a loop can do it in three or four lines.

The for loop is best when you know how many times to repeat. It has three parts: a starting value, a condition, and a change after each round. The while loop is best when you do not know the count in advance — it keeps running while its condition stays true. Be careful: if the condition never becomes false, the loop never stops.

#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

int main() {
    // for loop: print 1 to 5
    for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) {
        cout << i << " ";
    }
    cout << endl;

    // while loop: count down from 3
    int n = 3;
    while (n > 0) {
        cout << n << " ";
        n--;
    }
    return 0;
}

Practice idea: write a loop that prints the table of 7, from 7 × 1 to 7 × 10. Small practice like this builds strong basics.

Lesson 7 — Python: lists and dictionariesPython

A list in Python stores many values in one variable, in order. You write it with square brackets, and you can add, remove, or change items. Lists are perfect for things like student names, marks, or daily temperatures. You reach one item by its index, and remember: the first item is at index 0.

A dictionary stores data as key and value pairs, like a real dictionary where each word has a meaning. Instead of a number index, you use a name — the key — to find the value. Dictionaries are ideal for one student's record, where "name", "age", and "city" are keys.

# A list of marks
marks = [78, 85, 90, 66]
marks.append(72)          # add one more mark
print(marks[0])           # first mark: 78
print(len(marks))         # total marks: 5

# A dictionary for one student
student = {
    "name": "Sara",
    "age": 21,
    "city": "Larkana"
}
print(student["name"])    # Sara
student["course"] = "Python"   # add a new key
print(student)

Simple rule to remember: use a list when order matters and items are similar; use a dictionary when each value needs a clear name.

Lesson 8 — Data science and AI: the beginner roadmapData Science

Data science means learning useful facts from data, and AI means teaching computers to learn patterns from that data. This field looks big, but beginners can start step by step. You do not need to be a genius — you need a clear order and daily practice.

Step 1: Maths basics. Learn percentages, averages, basic statistics, and simple probability. Step 2: Python. Python is the main language of this field, so learn it well, including lists and dictionaries. Step 3: Data handling. Learn to clean and explore data with tools like spreadsheets first, then Python libraries such as pandas. Step 4: The machine learning idea. Understand it simply: we give the computer many examples, it finds patterns, and then it can make predictions on new data.

Step 5: Build small projects and a portfolio. Start with simple projects, for example analysing student marks, predicting house prices from sample data, or making charts from cricket scores. Save your work on GitHub. Two or three honest, finished projects teach you more than ten unfinished courses — and they help a lot for scholarships and jobs.

Scholarships

Bahar parhne ke khwab ko haqeeqat banane wale mashhoor scholarship programmes — Pakistani students ke liye. Har programme ki details aur dates hamesha us ki official website par confirm karein.

Find a scholarship

Filter by country, degree and funding — then always confirm dates on the official website before applying.

Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC)

Pakistani students and graduates can apply for Bachelor's, Master's and PhD studies at Chinese universities under this programme, arranged through the CSC online portal. It generally covers tuition and accommodation, and scholars generally receive a monthly living stipend under the programme rules. Practical tip: contact a professor in your field early and prepare a clear study plan before you apply.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

Stipendium Hungaricum

Pakistani students can apply for Bachelor's, Master's and PhD studies in Hungary through this programme, which Pakistan's HEC helps to nominate candidates for. It generally covers tuition, and scholars generally receive support for accommodation and living costs under the programme rules. Practical tip: apply through the HEC route as well as the programme portal, and keep your HAT or other required test scores ready.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters

Graduates from Pakistan can apply to these joint Master's programmes, where you study in at least two European countries with an international class. Selected scholars generally have their participation costs covered and generally receive a monthly allowance under the programme rules. Practical tip: you may apply to more than one programme, so read each programme's own page carefully and match your degree to its requirements.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

MEXT Scholarship — Japan

Pakistani students and graduates can apply for undergraduate and research (Master's and PhD) studies in Japan, mainly through the Embassy of Japan in Pakistan. It generally covers tuition, and scholars generally receive a monthly stipend and travel support under the programme rules. Practical tip: past papers of the written tests are your best preparation, so start practising English and your subject early.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

Brunei Darussalam Government Scholarship (BDGS)

Pakistani students can apply for Diploma, Bachelor's and Master's studies at universities in Brunei Darussalam under the Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship. It generally covers tuition, and scholars generally receive accommodation and a living allowance under the programme rules. Practical tip: this scheme has no application fee culture — apply only through the official Ministry of Foreign Affairs channel and beware of agents.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

HEC Pakistan — Scholarships Portal

The Higher Education Commission of Pakistan runs and announces many national and foreign scholarship schemes for Pakistani students, from undergraduate to PhD level. What each scheme covers depends on that scheme, and many international programmes on this site generally include tuition and living support. Practical tip: make your profile on the HEC portal once, keep it updated, and check the announcements page regularly so you never miss a call.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

Pakistani students can apply for Bachelor's, Master's and PhD studies at Turkish universities under the Türkiye Burslari programme. It generally covers tuition, and scholars generally receive a monthly stipend, accommodation support and a Turkish language course under the programme rules. Practical tip: your motivation letter matters a lot, so write it in your own honest words and connect it to your study field.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

Commonwealth Scholarships

Pakistani graduates can apply for Master's and PhD study in the United Kingdom under Commonwealth Scholarships, which are aimed at students from Commonwealth countries who could not otherwise afford to study there. These scholarships generally cover tuition fees and airfare, and scholars generally receive a living allowance under the programme rules. Practical tip: in Pakistan these are usually routed through HEC, so watch both the official scholarship site and HEC announcements.

Always confirm dates and rules on the official website before applying.

Official website →

How to prepare your documents

Almost every scholarship asks for the same standard set, so prepare it once and keep clear scanned copies ready: a valid passport, your degrees and transcripts, an updated CV, two recommendation letters from your teachers, and proof of English proficiency (for example IELTS, or an English proficiency certificate from your university where it is accepted). Preparing these early means you can apply quickly whenever a call opens.

About Me

I am Mutiu Rahman — a Bachelor of Computer Science (BS CS, University of Sindh, Jamshoro) and a teacher of C++ and Artificial Intelligence. I run StudySphere, the MR Academy platform, where students from Sindh and all over Pakistan prepare for SPSC, teaching jobs and screening tests with free MCQs, notes, books and past papers. I also offer online classes for test preparation and computer courses — if you want to prepare with me, just message on WhatsApp.

StudySphere is an educational platform built for students of Sindh and Pakistan who are preparing for government jobs, teaching jobs, screening tests and computer-based careers. It brings preparation material, past papers, practice tests and skill training together in one free place.

The platform is run by a teacher of computer science and AI who believes quality preparation should not depend on expensive academies. Every note and test here follows the real exam pattern, checked against official syllabi and past papers.

Our mission

Give every student, in every village and city, the same quality of preparation — learn, practice, prepare, succeed.

What we offer

Exam preparation, past papers, a PDF library, coding lessons, typing practice and auto-marked MCQ tests in English and Urdu, plus a daily quiz, word of the day, exam countdown and study timetable.

What is next

This link version is static and free to host. Student accounts and saved results would need hosting with a database, which is a separate step.

Privacy policy

This website does not collect, store or share your personal information. Practice tests, the typing test, the countdown and the timetable run entirely in your browser — your answers and entries are never sent anywhere.

Terms of use

All study material on StudySphere is provided free for personal exam preparation. Notes are summaries prepared for learning; for official syllabus and advertisement details, always confirm with IBA Sukkur STS, SPSC or the relevant board. You may share notes with fellow students, but please keep the StudySphere name on them.
